title: Minimum Length of Anagram Concatenation
summary: Given a string s that is a concatenation of anagrams of some string t, find the shortest possible length of t.
statement: Given a string s that is a concatenation of anagrams of some string t, find the shortest possible length of t.
constraints: s is a nonempty lowercase string known to be a concatenation of anagrams of some block.
Each aligned block must have the same character multiset, though its internal order may differ.
Return the smallest possible block length.
hints: A feasible block length must divide the total length, and all aligned blocks must share one frequency signature.
Test divisors from smallest upward against the first block’s character counts.
For each dividing size, compare Counter of every aligned slice with Counter(s[:size]); return the first success.
Divisor order guarantees minimality, and equal multisets are exactly the condition for every slice to be an anagram of one common block.
editorial: Divisor order guarantees minimality, and equal multisets are exactly the condition for every slice to be an anagram of one common block.

tests.explanation: Blocks ab and ba are anagrams, so the minimum length is two.
Each length-three block is abc, and no smaller divisor works, so the answer is three.
